reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output for a compliant finding; there is no over-flagging or invalid edit to correct — the rendered redline is byte-identical to the originals.

The cited text substantively supports the rule's purpose: Section 12.6.1(c) provides for transfer or destruction of all data and Information on termination, Section 12.7 (including 12.7.2 and 12.7.8) provides a reversion architecture with requested assistance, Section 12.10.2 gives a defined post-termination sell-off/wind-down period, and Section 12.5.2 gives the non-debtor Party (potentially us) a complete duplicate of or access to licensed IP and its embodiments. That is at or around the fallback level of orderly exit with data continuity.

The failed deterministic regex ('data return/transition present') is a phrasing artifact: this pharma development/option agreement expresses exit mechanics as reversion, data transfer/destruction and technology transfer rather than 'Customer Data export', so the check is weak evidence here and does not undercut the substance.

Directional analysis is correct: the termination data-transfer and assistance duties run against AbbVie (our party) in Harpoon's favour, and the counterparty holds no 'Customer Data' of ours requiring return; inserting a mirror data-return duty on Harpoon would gain us nothing and risks inviting reciprocal tightening of our own reversion obligations. Consistent with not flagging terms that benefit us.

Sub-elements short of the preferred wording (no fixed six-month assistance window, no written deletion certification) are appropriately noted in the rationale rather than raised as a deviation, per the classification semantics.
